key_insight: For shape-informed hemodynamic surrogates, active learning and finite-element physical consistency constraints are more effective during fine-tuning than early training.
engineering_relevance: The framework advances scalable, patient-specific prediction of aortic velocity and pressure fields toward real-time cardiovascular assessment.
method: Generate physiologically consistent CFD data from SynthAorta geometries using automatic boundary-condition adjustment.
Represent anatomies as displacement fields on a common reference geometry and train Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net surrogates.
Fine-tune using active learning and differentiable finite-element residual constraints.
evidence_signal: Peak-systolic evaluations report fine-tuning gains from gradient- and subspace-based acquisition, while out-of-distribution tests identify geometric parametrization support as the main limitation.
watch_item: Generalization remains constrained by the anatomical variability covered by the geometric parametrization; changing network architecture alone may not resolve this.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
